what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 3 of 3: Feed the gravity node the formation kernels. The gravity lane on main takes a lattice Green-function kernel as its node's input. Under the formation reading the candidates are now: (i) backward 2+1: a plane Green function times a level-time heat kernel (block 35, PR #8180); (ii) backward 3+1: sigma^2/(1 - |phi|^2), phi = (1 + sum_j e^{ik_j})/4, isotropic in the level plane's natural metric, with a one-sided response; (iii) light-cone 3+1: equal-time covariance 7 sigma^2/(2E(1 - E/14)) and static response 7/E(k) exactly (refereed; executed for the nonlinear law at 0.96-0.99). TASK: read the gravity lane's node statement on main (search docs/ for the generator kernel, the lattice Green function, 1/E(k); quote file and line), list the properties of the kernel it uses, and carry each candidate through the node: which properties hold, which fail, what the node's output becomes with chi = 7/E as input and sigma^2 = A(7 beta)/(7 beta) as the normalization, and what the coupling beta would have to be for the node's normalization. Exact checks of every identity you use. ROUND 2: the first round's attempts and referee reports are under probes/work/derive/<problem>/ and logs/probes/J:derive:*/ and logs/probes/J:confirm:J-derive-*/ (python3 probes/harvest.py lists them); what survived refereeing is stated below as GIVEN, what failed is stated as the gap. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/gravity-node-with-the-formation-kernels/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/gravity-node-with-the-formation-kernels/<name>/check.py"
